P1.evidence: Setter referenced by name — 'I already heard a couple of things from Derek, but to be honest, just love to hear everything from you.' Frame was the usual three parts and unusually garbled in delivery ('where are you at, that's why you want to go, see if we are really a fit there'). No explicit frame-agreement question; the prospect said 'Okay. Perfect.' unprompted. Open question ran verbatim.

P2.evidence: Weight asked directly ('how much do you weigh at the moment?' — 198) which is better than most of this batch, but age was volunteered and height never established. Occupation never asked at all: 'my business' and 'I have a coach in my business' both surfaced incidentally and neither was followed up, on a prospect being quoted $6,000. No health-conditions question. Injuries probed properly with a severity scale and a diurnal pattern ('on like a scale from one to ten' — five; 'in the morning... then throughout the day it loosens up'). The nutrition baseline is the best in the batch — protein grams, cheat meals, alcohol quantified at a couple of glasses daily, and the existing eating window. Sleep and energy both absent.

P3.evidence: Aesthetic goal pinned down including where he stores fat ('Where do you feel like you're storing it at the moment the most?' — 'More my gut'). The why was asked cleanly — 'why do you feel like you really want to get to those goals rather than just staying where you are?' — and produced the strongest self-articulation in the batch: 'you're either evolving or you're kind of slipping.' Future-pace ran and landed on snowboarding without fear of falling. Docked because the impact question was never asked — the children entered as small talk about their ages — and there was no drive-through to legacy and no reflect-back.

P4.evidence: Genuinely harder to run here because the prospect has not failed — he has been succeeding for two years and is shopping for an upgrade. Still, the gym-to-calisthenics switch was never interrogated, the earlier period of slipping in his thirties was raised by the prospect and never explored, and he was never asked to name a structural gap. The phase was applicable and largely skipped.

P5.evidence: The settle question ran — 'do you feel like you would be willing to settle for a life where it doesn't really get better because you sort of do continue with the work that you're doing at the moment?' — and the prospect deflected it with a long answer about his bar rising, never actually answering. The rep let it go rather than pressing. No two-year picture, no 'why not', no line in the sand. Against an optimizer with no pain and no urgency, this phase was the whole game and it was not played.

P6.evidence: Blocker sweep ran twice, once before the pitch and once after: 'do you feel like there's anything else that would stop you from getting leaner, getting more mobility, getting more muscle, strength, or does it then just come down to putting in the effort for you?' — 'I think it's just really putting in the effort.' And again after the three pillars: 'would there be anything that would stop you from getting to the results if you put in the effort there?' — 'I don't think so.' P6c is partial because the yes was conditional on effort rather than a commitment to proceed, and hesitation surfaced within seconds of the price.

P11.evidence: This is the notable one. The rep obtained a clear verbal yes on the $1,000 tier and then collected nothing: no link sent on the call, no payment taken, no agreement signed, no Skool invite. He let the prospect leave with 'I can send you a message with the sign-up link and then just let me know when you've done that.' The prospect had said he blocked off an hour and had to hop; the rep replied 'it usually takes like five minutes to set up' and then did not do it. P11b is N/A because the self-serve tier has no Trevor onboarding call.

objection_plays.detail: The dominant objection on the call and stated three separate times — 'I don't know if I would be able to follow through with one-on-one coaching', 'it might be different because my kids have been out for the summer... when they go back to school in August, it is going to open time up for me', and 'am I going to be able to actually swing that right now time-wise'. Not one OD move ran. No 'are you ever going to have another busy season', no 'things never slow down', no 'the longer you wait the harder this gets', no 'what if all you had to do was show up and everything else was handled' — which is precisely the answer to a man saying he lacks time to be coached. The rep did the reverse: he validated the objection and built a cheaper product around it.

One move ran, and ran early and well — the budget question before the price was revealed: 'What do you feel like you would want to put towards something like this for yourself?' The answer ('I'm not really sure what the market value is') should have been a green light. After the number landed, nothing: no isolation, no financial picture, no offer to break it up. The rep went straight from '$1,000 a month' hesitancy to the $1,000 tier.

'I need to think about it for a minute. But I'm open to it.' One move ran and it was the right one — 'what mainly comes up for you? Is that like the investment part?' — which correctly separated the money from the real blocker. None of the rest: no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you there', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no identity close.

SCRIPT GAP — 'I cannot absorb the value even if I buy it.' This is distinct from price, timing or doubt: the prospect believes in the programme and can afford it, but does not believe he has the hours to receive what he would be paying for. 'It's not that the value isn't there, it's like I'm not able to actually receive all the value.' Nothing in the playbook addresses a buyer whose constraint is capacity to consume rather than capacity to pay, and it is likely to be common among the business-owner ICP the company says it targets.

SCRIPT GAP — accountability experienced as pressure. 'I'm feeling a lot of pressure for the one-on-one right now. I don't want to add, I'm trying to have good growth without adding too much pressure.' The programme's central differentiator read as a liability to this buyer, and there is no scripted reframe for it. Worth capturing centrally: this is the second call in the batch where a prospect selected out of the coaching tier specifically to avoid being held accountable.

notes: Good discovery and a clean P6, undone at both ends. Phase 5 never ran against an optimizer with no pain, so there was nothing holding the $6,000 up. Then the OD play — the one play this call actually needed — was not run at all; the rep agreed with the timing objection and sold a $1,000 product around it. Worst of all, having earned a verbal yes he collected nothing: no link, no payment, no agreement, on a call where the prospect had five minutes and said he would do it. Coach P11 discipline first and the OD play second.
